**Finding submitted: T4C — deviation (high severity).**

**What the document does:** Paragraph 18 is the only exit mechanic. Para 18.1 (p0228) binds every Party for a 25-year Initial Period, with unilateral withdrawal permitted only at or after the end of that period on one year's notice. Para 18.2 (p0229) allows mid-term termination only by unanimous written agreement or a 90% Management Committee majority. Para 23 (p0255–p0257) is a for-cause default/capacity-reclamation mechanic, not a convenience right.

**Why it fails:** No Customer convenience exit exists in a 25-year term — expressly walk-away territory, failing both fallback Customer-notice elements. The counterparty side, however, is already acceptable: no other Party may unilaterally withdraw mid-term, and end-of-term withdrawal requires a full year's notice, so the "no Vendor convenience right during a committed term" element is met verbatim and was not re-drafted.

**Cure (preferred level, one insertion):** New Subparagraph 18.1A giving Teleglobe alone a convenience withdrawal right on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. The other Parties' rights are left untouched, and the capital-cost forfeiture sentence (p0233) — which is keyed to Subparagraph 18.1 and is handled under the liquidated-damages rule — was deliberately not edited, avoiding a double flag of the same money term while leaving no dangling cross-reference.
